title: Pounds or kilograms, how much fuel was loaded?
description: An aircraft needed 22300 kilograms of fuel but 22300 pounds were loaded. One pound is about 0.453 kilogram, so the fuel loaded is found by multiplying in parts and compared with the fuel needed. The close ties it to real life.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiply by a decimal in parts, then compare the result with the amount needed. Watch for students who forget that a pound and a kilogram are different units.

source: 22300 pounds of fuel were loaded, 1 pound is about 0.453 kg
video_script.why: The child can multiply decimals and now uses a decimal conversion between two units to compare amounts.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the pounds by the decimal in parts, add the parts, and compare with the kilograms needed.
video_script.anchor: An aircraft that was loaded with fuel counted in pounds when kilograms were needed.
video_script.payoff_line: Change the unit first, then compare the amounts

final_answer.value: About 10102 kg, about half of what was needed
final_answer.spoken: about ten thousand one hundred two kilograms, about half of what was needed

hold_back: About 10102 kg, about half of what was needed
maths_rules: half of 22300 is 11150, and 10102 is a little less than half of the 22300 kg needed
video_script.design: The loaded pounds and the needed kilograms are written in two different colours. The decimal 0.453 is split into 0.4, 0.05 and 0.003, each part is multiplied, and the parts are added. The result is placed against half of the amount needed.

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, multiply the pounds by each part of the decimal.
<bookmark mark='p1'/>Twenty two thousand three hundred times four tenths is eight thousand nine hundred twenty.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>Times five hundredths is one thousand one hundred fifteen.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>Times three thousandths is sixty six point nine.

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add the three products with the decimal point in one column.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>That makes ten thousand one hundred one point nine.
<bookmark mark='round'/>This is about ten thousand one hundred two kilograms.

narration: <bookmark mark='tank'/>In real life, mixing up pounds and kilograms left an aircraft with about half of its fuel.
